text.p: Bradesco, Brazil's largest private bank, posted a record 824.5 million reais net profit in 1996 due to increased earnings from subsidiaries, higher banking fees and fewer bad debts, the bank's president said.

"Profits came mostly from earnings from subsidiaries, particularly from the insurance unit, which includes capitalization and pension plans," Bradesco's president Lazaro Brandao told Reuters in a telephone interview.

Brandao said 89 percent of the bank's net profit came from gains with subsidiaries, including insurance and credit card units, while 11 percent was operational profit. He said that profits at the insurance subsidiary rose 10 percent to 350 million reais last year.
For 1997, Bradesco chief said he expects the bank to show even better results but on higher operating revenues, particularly from consumer credit operations.
"We are ready to increase our consumer credit operations," he said, adding that banks this year are more willing to lend on eased concerns over high consumer and corporate defaults.
"Banks will continue to be selective, but consumer credit operations will grow," he said.

Higher revenues from banking fees and a decrease in the bank's bad debt portfolio also contributed to Bradesco's net profit, which rose 52.6 percent over 1995 and was reportedly the highest ever announced by a private Brazilian company.
Revenues from banking fees rose 26.6 percent to 1.165 billion reais, while the bank's bad debts portfolio fell 33.06 percent to 407 million reais, the bank said in a statement.
It said those bad debts are covered by loan-loss provisions of 661 million reais.
Bradesco showed a 15 percent return on equity, the highest rate since 1989 when the bank's return on equity was 21 percent.
"Historically, the bank's return on equity ranges between 12 percent and 14 percent," said Brandao.
The bank's net worth rose 12.76 percent to 5.460 billion reais in 1996, while its total assets increased 17.97 percent to 38.766 billion reais in the same period.
Bradesco raised last year 50.6 billion reais, a rise of 38.34 percent, the statement said.
The bank's investment funds totalled 13.717 billion reais, while its savings accounts amounted to 10 billion reais, a rise of 21 percent when compared with 1995.
Brandao also said the bank remained cautious about the bank's expenses. Last year, the bank's staff fell to 46,000 employees from 52,000.
He said Bradesco could continue reducing personnel costs but the "adjustment should be smoother."
